newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, bellies end lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, bellies end lower on profit taking.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures posted moderate to sharp losses at the close, mostly under pressure from profit taking, floor traders said.
"All the people that have been getting in the market this week were massive sellers today (Thursday)," one commission house trader said.
Both locals and other larger speculators were active sellers throughout the session, pit sources said.
"The packer started to lose money on his cutout Wednesday, so he's not having a big Saturday kill after all," one cash-connected trader said.
Those ideas that packers would not be aggressive buyers of cash hogs Friday scared some speculators out of the market and pushed cash hog calls lower for Friday, floor sources said.
Although the USDA showed higher pork cutout values on Wednesday, packers were actually selling products at lower prices, one cash-connected source said.
Cash hog markets in the Midwest had traded from 0.50 to 1.50 per cwt higher on good packer demand, but that demand was expected to diminish somewhat on Friday, traders said.
Commission houses were noted buyers of June and sellers of February hogs, pit sources said.

Locals taking profits pushed pork belly futures to a sharply lower close. Another bearish factor in the market included Wednesday's larger-than-expected slaughter of 370,000 head, analysts and traders said.
December hogs settled at 54.55 cents per lb, down 0.550, and February closed down 0.800 at 74.150 cent. Other contracts were down 0.400 to 0.600 cent.
February pork bellies closed down 2.250 at 68.30 cent and other contracts were down 2.000 to 2.925 cent.
